suggested_fixes.reason: The note attributes the double-clear reachability to the DataValue_copy memcpy aliasing dst->value onto src's data pointer. Reading DataValue_copy, the memcpy is immediately followed by UA_Variant_init(&dst->value), which zeroes dst->value.data before Variant_copy allocates a fresh array. So the value-variant alias from the memcpy is undone right away and is not what makes the freed array reachable twice. The actual double-read comes from the same variant object being cleared twice during nested error unwinding (inner DataValue_copy failure cleanup frees the array, then the outer UA_Array_copy/UA_copy failure cleanup re-traverses it) while Variant_clear leaves p->data dangling. This is a prose/mechanism refinement only; the step's file/function/line/code are correct and non-blocking.
suggested_fixes.suggested_replacement: DataValue_copy bulk-copies src into dst then re-inits and re-copies dst->value; on the nested copy failure the cleanup frees the variant's element array. Because Variant_clear (step 8) never nulls p->data, the same variant object is then cleared a second time during the outer copy's error unwinding, re-traversing the freed array. The un-nulled dangling p->data — not the transient memcpy alias — is what makes the freed region reachable from a second clear.
